I’ve watched it 3x already and highly recommend it. Here is the description: “An intimate and raw look at the transformational journey of two combat veterans suffering from severe trauma (PTSD) as they abandon pharmaceuticals to seek relief through the mind-expanding world of psychedelics.” Even if you don’t watch the film, [the two-minute trailer](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/qdurox544u7hd04kwie/pdaeh9hdo4pnq8/aHR0cHM6Ly92aW1lby5jb20vb25kZW1hbmQvZnJvbXNob2NrdG9hd2U=) is worth checking out.

bullets.title: I Wrote This Book Because I Love You: Essays
bullets.creator: Tim Kreider
bullets.note: com](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/qdurox544u7hd04kwie/8qfqhoh3no7mr8/aHR0cDovL3RpbWtyZWlkZXIuY29tLw==)). Many of you know that Tim’s [_We Learn Nothing_](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/qdurox544u7hd04kwie/lztehmh47ld8xg/aHR0cDovL3d3dy5hdWRpYmxlLmNvbS9wZC9CaW9zLU1lbW9pcnMvV2UtTGVhcm4tTm90aGluZy1BdWRpb2Jvb2svQjAwU05UUVU5Sw==), his dazzling collection of humor and insight, is one of the few books in the [Tim Ferriss Book Club](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/qdurox544u7hd04kwie/dnceh0hkne2l2z/aHR0cDovL3d3dy5hdWRpYmxlLmNvbS9tdC9UaW1zQm9va3M_YnBfdWE9eWVzJnNvdXJjZV9jb2RlPUFVREdCV1MwOTA4MTQ5QVVX). To get a taste, you can listen to one of my favorite chapters, “**Lazy: A Manifesto**,” [**in this short 20-minute episode of the podcast**](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/qdurox544u7hd04kwie/7xs7h8h859xrxk/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDE1LzA0LzAzL2xhenktYS1tYW5pZmVzdG8vP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9Y29udmVydGtpdCZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWNvbnZlcnRraXQmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTViZg==)**.** I’ve been eager to revisit Tim’s work, and I’m now digging into [his latest collection of essays](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/qdurox544u7hd04kwie/m6a7h5h9z3ld4l/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYW1hem9uLmNvbS9Xcm90ZS1UaGlzLUJvb2stQmVjYXVzZS1Mb3ZlL2RwLzE0NzY3Mzg5OTgv). Tim’s fans include people like filmmaker Judd Apatow ([@JuddApatow](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/qdurox544u7hd04kwie/xdbph6hz0e454z/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9KdWRkQXBhdG93)), who gave him the blurb of all blurbs: “Tim Kreider’s writing is heartbreaking, brutal and hilarious—usually at the same time. He can do in a few pages what I need several hours of screen time and tens of millions to accomplish. And he does it better. Come to think of it, I’d rather not do a blurb. I am beginning to feel bad about myself.”
